Use hasClear when the datetime is optional so the user can reset it.

Dialog.name: Dialog
Dialog.description:
Dialog displays a modal overlay that blocks interaction with the page until the user responds. Use it for delete confirmations, edit forms, terms acceptance, or any decision that should not be skipped.

For cases where you want to show a dialog without managing open state, use the `useImperativeDialog` hook: call `dialog.show(content)` and render `dialog.element` in your tree.

bestPractices.description: Choose the right purpose: info for dismissable content, form to prevent accidental backdrop dismissal, required when the user must respond.
Include a clear title in the header so users immediately understand what the dialog is asking.
Use purpose="form" for dialogs with inputs so the user can't accidentally lose data by clicking the backdrop.
Keep dialogs focused on a single task; if the content grows beyond what fits, consider a full page instead.
Use a dialog for simple messages that could be shown inline or as a toast notification.
Nest dialogs inside other dialogs; restructure the flow into steps within a single dialog instead.
Use the fullscreen variant for simple confirmations; it is meant for complex content like editors or long forms.

Divider.name: Divider
Divider.description: A visual separator that divides content into distinct sections. Use to create clear boundaries between groups of related content, or to demarcate interactive regions within a layout.

Add a label to the divider when sections need a visible category heading.
Overuse dividers; rely on spacing and layout to separate content when possible.

props.name: xstyle

DropdownMenu.name: DropdownMenu
DropdownMenu.description: A dropdown menu that displays a list of actionable items in a popup triggered by a button. Use to present action options as a next step in a process, or to offer contextual actions without cluttering the interface.

bestPractices.description: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented so users can scan options quickly.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
Use a DropdownMenu for navigation; use a navigation component instead.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

props.description: Props for the trigger button (Button props except onClick).

props.name: items

props.description: Callback fired when the trigger button is clicked.

props.name: hasChevron
props.description: Whether to show a chevron icon on the trigger button. Set to false for icon-only triggers.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom render function for each item in the list.

DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.name: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
DropdownMenuCheckboxItem.description: A checkable menu item (role="menuitemcheckbox") that toggles an independent boolean. Use for on/off options inside a DropdownMenu; for a one-of-N choice use DropdownMenuRadioGroup.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text identifying the item.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `npx pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the item is checked. Controlled; pair with onChange.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired with the next checked state when the item is toggled.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the item is disabled. Disabled items stay focusable (via aria-disabled) so they remain discoverable by keyboard and assistive technology, but activation is blocked.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether toggling the item closes the menu. Checkbox items default to staying open so several can be toggled in a single session.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label and description, such as a keyboard shortcut hint or badge.

DropdownMenuItem.name: DropdownMenuItem
DropdownMenuItem.description: Helper component for custom item rendering with consistent styling.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Additional content rendered after the label and description.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

DropdownMenuRadioGroup.name: DropdownMenuRadioGroup
DropdownMenuRadioGroup.description: A single-select group of radio menu items (role="group" of menuitemradio). Owns the selected value and lays its items out with the menu's inter-item gap.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected value in the group. Pass undefined when nothing is selected yet.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the selected value changes.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the group. Required (or aria-labelledby) so screen readers announce the radios as a named set, e.g. "Sort by".

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of an element that labels the group, as an alternative to aria-label.

props.name: hasCloseOnSelect
props.description: Whether selecting a value closes the menu. Radio items default to closing on selection (a single-choice commit).

props.name: children
props.description: The DropdownMenuRadioItems that make up the group.

DropdownMenuRadioItem.name: DropdownMenuRadioItem
DropdownMenuRadioItem.description: A single option in a DropdownMenuRadioGroup (role="menuitemradio"). Must be used inside a DropdownMenuRadioGroup.

props.name: value
props.description: The value this item represents within its group. The group's value matches against this to determine the checked state.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text identifying the option.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `npx pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this individual radio item is disabled. Disabled items stay focusable (via aria-disabled) so they remain discoverable by keyboard and assistive technology, but selection is blocked.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to render after the label and description, such as a badge or metadata.

DropdownMenuSubMenu.name: DropdownMenuSubMenu
DropdownMenuSubMenu.description: A single menu row that reveals a nested flyout of its own items. The row adopts DropdownMenuItem semantics (label / icon / description / isDisabled); its children become the flyout content. Opens inline-end with viewport auto-flip; Right/Enter/Space opens and focuses the first item, Left/Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger (Right/Left swap in RTL). For data-driven menus, give a menu item a nested `items` array instead of using this component directly.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary label text for the trigger row.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon to display before the label. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary description text displayed below the label.

props.name: children
props.description: The flyout menu items — the same components used at the top level (DropdownMenuItem, nested DropdownMenuSubMenu, selectable items).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: A disabled submenu renders its trigger row but never opens the flyout.

props.name: hasSpinner
props.description: Show a spinner in place of the caret, e.g. while a lazy submenu’s children are loading.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Fixed flyout width. Defaults to sizing to its content (min 160px).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the flyout opens or closes.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the trigger row. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

EmptyState.name: EmptyState
EmptyState.description: EmptyState shows a placeholder when a content area has no data. Use it for empty lists, zero search results, first-time setups, or cleared inboxes. Always include a title and a next step so the user is not stuck.

bestPractices.description: Include a clear title and a call-to-action button so users know how to proceed.
Use an illustration or icon that reinforces the context of the empty state.
Use the compact variant inside cards or sidebars where space is limited.
Leave an empty state without guidance; always explain what happened and what the user can do next.
Use a generic message like "No data"; be specific about what is empty and why.
Use an EmptyState for error messages that require immediate action; use a Banner instead.

props.name: title
props.description: Primary message rendered as an <h3> heading inside the empty state.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional secondary text providing additional context below the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon or illustration displayed above the title; rendered as decorative (aria-hidden="true").

props.name: actions
props.description: Optional action buttons displayed below the description, laid out horizontally by default and stacked vertically when isCompact is true.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Controls only the rendered HTML heading tag (h1-h6) so the title fits the document outline. This is a semantic change for accessibility and does not change the visual size of the title, which stays fixed regardless of level.

props.name: isCompact
props.description: Enables the compact variant with reduced spacing for constrained content areas.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Field.name: Field
Field.description: Field is a low-level wrapper for custom, native, or third-party controls that do not already provide field label, description, and status UI. Use it when you need the Field shell around a control you own; use styled Pharos inputs like TextInput, Typeahead, and Select directly when they already expose label, description, and validation props.

bestPractices.description: Wrap custom controls, native inputs, or third-party widgets that need labeling, helper text, optional/required indicators, or validation status.
Always provide a label for accessibility, even if visually hidden with isLabelHidden.
Use inputID and descriptionID to connect the label and description to the inner control with htmlFor and aria-describedby.
Nest Field around styled inputs such as TextInput, Typeahead, Select, DateInput, or TextArea; those components already render their own Field shell.
Use the attached status variant on non-bordered controls such as sliders, switches, or checkboxes; use detached so the message does not overlap the control.
Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field.
Hide the label without providing an alternative way for the user to understand the field purpose.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the field (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: inputID
props.description: ID for the input element (used for the label htmlFor attribute).

props.name: children
props.description: The input or control to render.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the associated input is disabled. Propagates disabled styling to the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: descriptionID
props.description: ID for the description element (use for aria-describedby on the input).

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required (mutually exclusive with isOptional).

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon to display before the label text. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text to display in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator with type and optional message. When message is set, displays a colored status box. messageID is for wiring aria-describedby on the input.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message renders relative to the input. Attached overlaps the input border; detached floats below.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Prefer this over setting width via xstyle/className/style, which only size the inner control box.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the root element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s) appended to the root element. Prefer xstyle for StyleX deduplication.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the root element. Takes priority over StyleX inline styles.

FieldLabel.name: FieldLabel
FieldLabel.description: Standalone label component with optional/required indicators and tooltip support.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text.

props.name: inputID
props.description: ID of the input this label is for.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the associated input is disabled.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show "Optional" indicator.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Show "Required" indicator.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon before the label text. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text for info icon at end of label.

FieldStatus.name: FieldStatus
FieldStatus.description: FieldStatus renders validation feedback for fields and field-like controls. Use it directly for custom controls that need the same error, warning, or success presentation as Field.

bestPractices.description: Use attached status below bordered inputs when the message belongs to that input.
Use detached status for controls like checkboxes, switches, and custom controls where overlap would be visually awkward.
Use FieldStatus for general alerts or page-level notices; use Banner or Toast instead.

props.name: type
props.description: Status type.

props.name: message
props.description: Status message text.

props.name: id
props.description: ID for aria-describedby association.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant: attached overlaps the input, detached floats below.

FileInput.name: FileInput
FileInput.description: FileInput provides file upload with optional drag-and-drop support. Use it for single or multiple file selection with built-in validation for file type, size, and count. Pair with validation status for upload feedback.

bestPractices.description: Always specify an accept prop to guide users toward valid file types.
Use maxSize and maxFiles to prevent oversized uploads; the component handles validation and error display automatically.
Add a description to communicate constraints like file size limits or accepted formats.
Use changeAction for immediate upload workflows that benefit from optimistic UI.
Don't use FileInput for directory or folder uploads; that is not supported in v1.
Don't avoid dropzone mode unless space is constrained; drag-and-drop is the expected interaction for file uploads.
Don't wrap a disabled FileInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the file input.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected file(s). Controlled component.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when files are selected or removed.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async change action (React 19 transitions pattern). Use for immediate upload on file selection.

props.name: accept
props.description: Accepted file types. Uses the HTML accept attribute format (e.g. "image/*", ".pdf,.doc").

props.name: isMultiple
props.description: Whether multiple files can be selected. When true, value and onChange use File[] instead of File.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Maximum file size in bytes. Files exceeding this are rejected with an error status.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: Maximum number of files (only applies when isMultiple is true).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and adds a screen-reader-only "Required" description to the trigger (assistive tech does not reliably announce aria-required on the trigger). Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the trigger focusable via aria-disabled (opening the file picker stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled FileInput in Tooltip; disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no file is selected.

props.name: mode
props.description: Visual mode. 'input' is a compact inline style; 'dropzone' is a larger area with drag-and-drop support.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

FormLayout.name: FormLayout
FormLayout.description: A layout container that arranges form fields with consistent spacing and direction. FormLayout handles where fields go, not state or submission. Wrap it in a <form> for that. Supports vertical (default), horizontal, and horizontal-labels directions, and can be nested to mix them.

bestPractices.description: Stack fields vertically for most forms. It's the easiest to scan top to bottom.
Nest a horizontal FormLayout inside a vertical one when fields naturally pair up, like First Name + Last Name or City + State + ZIP.
Use horizontal-labels for settings pages where labels sit beside their inputs.
Use FormLayout for form state or submission. It's just layout. Wrap it in a <form> for that.
Put unrelated fields side by side in a horizontal layout. Save it for fields that belong together.
Nest horizontal-labels inside another FormLayout. It uses CSS Grid and needs to be the outermost container.

props.name: direction
props.description: Controls field arrangement. Vertical stacks top-to-bottom, horizontal arranges left-to-right with equal flex-grow, and horizontal-labels uses CSS Grid with labels to the left of inputs (collapses to vertical on narrow viewports <=480px).

props.name: children
props.description: Form fields to arrange. Accepts Pharos inputs (TextInput, Selector, etc.) and Field-wrapped custom controls.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Grid.name: Grid
Grid.description: A CSS grid layout container for arranging children in rows and columns. Use Grid for card galleries, dashboards, and any multi-column layout. Supports fixed column counts and responsive columns that reflow based on available width.

bestPractices.description: Use responsive columns for layouts that should adapt to screen size: `columns={{minWidth: 280}}`.
Cap the column count with `max` to prevent rows from getting too wide on large screens.
Use `repeat: 'fill'` (the default) for consistent item widths. Use `'fit'` when items should stretch to fill leftover space.
Write manual CSS grid; Grid handles spacing and responsive behavior for you.
Use `HStack` with wrapping for grids; use Grid instead.
Track templates use CSS-variable indirection (not raw inline styles), so `xstyle` overrides of `gridTemplateColumns` (including inside `@media` queries) take effect.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column configuration. Use a number for fixed columns (e.g. `columns={3}`). Use an object for responsive columns: `minWidth` sets the minimum column width in px, `repeat` controls track behavior (`"fill"` preserves empty tracks for consistent widths, `"fit"` collapses empty tracks so items stretch; defaults to `"fill"`), and `max` caps the maximum number of columns.

props.name: minChildWidth
props.description: Deprecated: use `columns={{minWidth: 280}}` instead. Minimum item width in px; enables responsive auto-fit.

props.name: width
props.description: Container width. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: height
props.description: Container height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Maximum container width. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: minHeight
props.description: Minimum container height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing between all items.

props.name: rowGap
props.description: Row spacing; overrides `gap` for the row axis.

props.name: columnGap
props.description: Column spacing; overrides `gap` for the column axis.

props.name: align
props.description: Vertical alignment of items.

props.name: justify
props.description: Horizontal alignment of items.

props.name: children
props.description: Grid content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

GridSpan.name: GridSpan
GridSpan.description: Grid item that spans multiple columns or rows.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns to span; use `'full'` to span the entire row.

props.name: rows
props.description: Rows to span.

props.name: children
props.description: Content.

HoverCard.name: HoverCard
HoverCard.description: HoverCard shows additional information when the user hovers or focuses a trigger element. Use it for profile cards, link summaries, or inline definitions where the user needs more context without navigating away.

bestPractices.description: Keep content supplementary; hover cards should enhance understanding without blocking the primary workflow.
Provide a dashed underline on text triggers so users know the element is hoverable.
Use the hook API (useHoverCard) when you need more control over timing or placement.
Place critical actions or required information inside a hover card; users may miss content that only appears on hover.
Use a hover card when a simple Tooltip or Popover would suffice.
Use a HoverCard for content the user must interact with; it disappears when the cursor leaves.

Nest a HoverCard whose content has block elements directly inside phrasing-only contexts such as a

,

) instead.

Icon.name: Icon
Icon.description: Icons are small visual symbols that represent actions, objects, or concepts. They improve scannability and reinforce meaning alongside text. Supports both direct SVG components and semantic icon names that adapt to the active theme.

bestPractices.description: Use semantic icon names when available; they adapt to theme changes automatically.
Pair icons with text labels for accessibility; icon-only elements need an accessible label.
For a meaningful standalone icon (no adjacent text), give it an accessible name via the `label` prop: it sets role="img" + aria-label and unhides the icon.
Use color tokens for icon colors, not hardcoded hex values.
Be mindful of context; decorative icons in compact components can distract rather than help.
Use icons as the sole means of conveying meaning; always provide a text alternative.
Resize icons with arbitrary pixel values; use the provided size props.
Mix icon styles (e.g. outline and filled) within the same context.
Render raw SVG elements; always wrap in Icon for consistent sizing and color.
Pass a `name` prop; Icon uses `icon` (not `name`) to specify which icon to render.

props.name: icon
props.description: Semantic icon name or SVG component. Valid semantic names: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. For any icon not in this list, pass an SVG component directly (e.g. import from lucide-react or @heroicons/react). Note: this prop is called `icon`, not `name`.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant mapped to Pharos icon color tokens.

props.name: size
props.description: Icon size.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for a MEANINGFUL, standalone icon (a status glyph or icon-only indicator with no adjacent text). Setting it exposes the icon to screen readers as role="img" with this text as the accessible name (aria-label) and removes the default aria-hidden. Omit it (default) for decorative icons and the icon stays hidden from assistive tech (aria-hidden="true"). This is the accessible-name / alt-text prop for icons: one prop instead of manually setting aria-label + role + aria-hidden. An empty string is treated as decorative. Do not set it when an interactive parent (Button, IconButton, link) already names the control.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for customization (color, size, opacity). Folded into the icon's own stylex.props() call so it composes with the base color/size styles. Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

IconButton.name: IconButton
IconButton.description: A button that shows only an icon with no visible text. Use IconButton in toolbars, table rows, and compact UI where space is tight and the icon is universally understood.

bestPractices.description: Make the aria-label specific: a trash icon labeled "Delete conversation" is clearer than just "Delete" for screen readers.
Add a tooltip: even a gear icon can mean Settings, Preferences, or Configure.
Use ghost in toolbars and dense areas to reduce visual clutter.
Use IconButton if the action isn't obvious from the icon alone; use Button with text.
Skip the tooltip; label only reaches screen readers, sighted users need the hover hint.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label. Used as aria-label (not rendered as visible text).

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element rendered inside the button.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth. The most common FAB shape is an icon-only button, so raise it with `low`/`med`/`high` for a floating action button. `none` is the default flat button.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner and disables interaction.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the button.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Standard click handler.

props.name: clickAction
props.description: Async click handler with automatic loading state.

InputGroup.name: InputGroup
InputGroup.description: InputGroup connects an input with prefix/suffix addons in a single visual unit. Use it for URL fields, currency inputs, search fields with action buttons, or any input that needs contextual decorations.

bestPractices.description: Use text addons to show units, prefixes, or suffixes that clarify the input format (e.g., "$", "kg", "https://").
Use InputGroupText for static prefixes/suffixes like "$", "kg", or "https://".
Use InputGroup with compatible single-line inputs: TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Selector, and MultiSelector.
Keep each inner input's label specific; grouped inputs automatically combine the group label with their own label and inherit the group description/status context.
Don't put multiple text inputs in one group; use separate fields instead.
Don't use InputGroup for unrelated inputs; it's for a single input with decorations.
Don't use InputGroup with TextArea, Slider, Switch, CheckboxInput, or RadioList.

props.name: children
props.description: InputGroupText and compatible input children: TextInput, NumberInput, TimeInput, DateInput, Typeahead, Selector, or MultiSelector.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text between label and input group.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disable the entire group.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Show "(optional)" indicator.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Mark the field as required.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for inputs in the group.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator applied to the group border.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text at the end of the label.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector.

InputGroupText.name: InputGroupText
InputGroupText.description: A prefix or suffix text element rendered inside InputGroup. Displays text or icons.

props.name: children
props.description: Text or icon content.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for customization.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s).

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles.

InternationalizationProvider.name: InternationalizationProvider
InternationalizationProvider.description: Wraps your app to set the active locale and (optionally) merge additional translation catalogs + per-locale overrides. Pharos components inside the subtree resolve their strings against this context. If no provider is present, components fall back to the shipped English defaults.

bestPractices.description: Use shipped Pharos locale catalogs from `@pharos-ds/core/locales/*` when one exists for your target locale.
Use a same-shape local catalog only when Pharos has not shipped that locale yet or you are testing in-progress translations.
Use real BCP 47 tags such as `fr`, `pt-BR`, or `ar`; regional locales fall back to their base language before English.
Cast custom catalog maps to `any`; the i18n package exports `MessagesByLocale` and `Catalog` for local catalog typing.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 language tag for the active locale (e.g. "en", "pt", "pt-BR", "zh-Hans"). Regional tags fall back to their base language, then to the shipped "en" catalog.

props.name: messages
props.description: Optional map of BCP 47 tag to translation catalog. Import shipped catalogs from `@pharos-ds/core/locales/*`; the shipped "en" catalog is always available and does not need to be listed here.

props.name: overrides
props.description: Sparse per-locale key overrides applied on top of shipped defaults. Overrides are locale-keyed so a runtime locale swap picks up the correct set.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the internationalization provider.

Item.name: Item
Item.description: A single, flexible item primitive that unifies the "start content + label + description + end content" pattern across Pharos. Use it wherever you need a structured row: dropdown menus, selectors, contact lists, notifications, file browsers, and activity feeds.

bestPractices.description: Use named slots (startContent, label, description, endContent) for the common layout. These cover the 80% case.
Use density="compact" for menus and dense lists, "balanced" for standard rows, and "spacious" for roomier layouts.
Set labelLines and descriptionLines to control truncation when content length varies.
Use align="start" when start or end content is taller than a single line of text.
Don't nest interactive elements (buttons, links) inside an interactive Item; it creates confusing focus and click targets.
Don't use Item for navigation between views; use proper navigation components instead.
Don't add read/unread or inbox-specific behavior directly; compose a thin wrapper like PreviewItem instead.

Kbd.name: Kbd
Kbd.description: Renders a keyboard shortcut as styled key badges. Use Kbd in tooltips, menus, and help text to show key combinations.

bestPractices.description: Place shortcuts near the action they trigger: in a tooltip, menu item, or inline instruction.
Use mod instead of ctrl or cmd; it automatically adapts to the user's platform.
Use Kbd as the only way to discover an action; shortcuts should supplement visible controls, not replace them.

props.name: keys
props.description: Keyboard shortcut string. Use "+" to separate keys. Special keys: mod (Cmd on Mac), ctrl, alt, shift, enter, backspace, escape, tab, up, down, left, right.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

Layout.name: Layout
Layout.description: Layout provides composable components for building structured page shells with header, sidebar, content, and footer slots. Use Layout for full app layouts and HStack/VStack for simple directional stacking.

bestPractices.description: Use Layout for page shells that need distinct zones like header, sidebar(s), content, and footer.
Use HStack and VStack for simple directional stacking within a content area.
Use Layout for simple stacking layouts; use HStack or VStack instead.
Nest multiple Layout components; use one per page shell and compose content within its slots.

props.name: content
props.description: Main content area (center). Children passed to `<Layout>` render here too: `<Layout>{main}</Layout>` is shorthand for `<Layout content={main} />`.

props.name: header
props.description: Header slot.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer slot.

props.name: start
props.description: Start panel (left in LTR).

props.name: end
props.description: End panel (right in LTR).

props.name: height
props.description: Height behavior: fill the container or grow with content.

props.name: children
props.description: Content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale. Overrides the default padding from the layout container.

props.name: isScrollable
props.description: Enable scrollable overflow.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

LayoutFooter.name: LayoutFooter
LayoutFooter.description: Bottom bar for action bars, pagination, and status bars.

props.name: children
props.description: Footer content.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Border at top edge.

props.name: height
props.description: Footer height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

LayoutHeader.name: LayoutHeader
LayoutHeader.description: Top bar for page titles, app bars, and toolbars.

props.name: children
props.description: Header content.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Border at bottom edge.

props.name: height
props.description: Header height. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

LayoutPanel.name: LayoutPanel
LayoutPanel.description: Sidebar for navigation, settings, or inspector panels.

props.name: children
props.description: Panel content.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Border on the appropriate edge.

props.name: padding
props.description: Internal padding using the spacing scale. Overrides the default padding from the layout container.

props.name: isScrollable
props.description: Enable scrollable overflow.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark element.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA landmark role.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the panel. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is. Ignored when resizable is provided; the hook controls width.

props.name: resizable
props.description: Resize props from useResizable(). When provided, the hook drives the panel width and a ResizeHandle should be placed adjacent to the panel.

Lightbox.name: Lightbox
Lightbox.description: A fullscreen overlay for viewing images and videos at full resolution. Supports single-item and gallery modes with prev/next navigation, optional zoom and pan for images, and native video controls.

bestPractices.description: Always provide alt text for every image for screen reader accessibility.
Use gallery mode with onIndexChange for multi-image sets.
Enable hasZoom only when viewing high-resolution images that benefit from close inspection.
Use the lightbox for non-image content; it is specialized for images.
Nest interactive content inside captions; keep them plain text.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Whether the lightbox is open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the lightbox open state changes.

props.name: media
props.description: Media to display. Pass a single object for one item, or an array for gallery mode with prev/next navigation. Each item is {src: string, alt: string, caption?: ReactNode, type?: 'image' | 'video'}; type defaults to 'image', and zoom/pan is disabled for 'video'.

props.name: index
props.description: Current index in gallery mode (when media is an array).

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Callback when the gallery index changes via prev/next navigation.

props.name: hasZoom
props.description: Enable zoom on double-click (images only). When zoomed, drag to pan.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be stylex.create() value.

Link.name: Link
Link.description: A styled anchor for inline and standalone text navigation. Supports external links, underline variants, tooltips, and custom link components for router integration. Use it for navigating between pages or to external URLs.

bestPractices.description: Write descriptive, concise link text that clearly communicates the destination.
Set `isStandalone` when the link appears outside of inline text, so it receives proper base font sizing.

Only set `label` when the link content is not descriptive text (e.g. an icon-only link). For text links, the visible text is already the accessible name; adding `label` overrides it for screen readers, which is harmful.
Use Link for actions that do not navigate; use a Button instead.
Use generic text like "click here" or "read more"; describe the destination.
Set `label` on text links; `aria-label` prevents assistive technology from reading the actual link content.

LinkProvider.name: LinkProvider
LinkProvider.description: Wraps your app to replace the default <a> tag with a framework-specific link component (e.g. Next.js Link) for client-side routing across all Pharos components.

props.name: component
props.description: Link component to use for all link elements in the subtree (e.g. Next.js Link).

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the link provider.

List.name: List
List.description: A vertical collection of items with consistent spacing, dividers, and optional markers. Supports headers, icons, avatars, badges, and interactive items with click or link behavior. Use it to display ordered or unordered groups of related content.

bestPractices.description: Provide a header to label the list and give context to screen readers.
Use start and end content slots to add icons, avatars, or badges to each item.
Place interactive elements inside an interactive list item; it creates nested click targets and confusing focus behavior.
Use a list for a single item or for laying out unrelated content; lists imply a meaningful collection.
Mix clickable and non-clickable items in the same list without clear visual distinction.

props.name: children
props.description: List items (ListItem components).

props.name: density
props.description: Spacing density for items.

props.name: hasDividers
props.description: Show dividers between items.

props.name: header
props.description: Header content, associated with the list via aria-labelledby.

props.name: listStyle
props.description: List marker style. 'decimal' renders an <ol> element instead of <ul>.

props.name: start
props.description: Starting number for ordered lists (listStyle='decimal'). Sets the CSS counter to begin at this value.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

ListItem.name: ListItem
ListItem.description: List item with label, description, start/end content slots, and interactive patterns.

props.name: label
props.description: Primary text.

props.name: description
props.description: Secondary content below the label. A plain string gets single-line truncation automatically; a ReactNode lets child components control their own wrapping and line-clamp behavior.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Content rendered before the label area (e.g. icon, avatar).

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label area (e.g. badge, chevron).

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler; enables the invisible button pattern.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL; enables the invisible anchor pattern.

props.name: target
props.description: Link target attribute, only applicable when href is provided. target="_blank" automatically adds noopener noreferrer.

props.name: rel
props.description: Link relationship tokens. noopener noreferrer are merged automatically for target="_blank".

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disabled state; sets aria-disabled on the item.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Selected state; sets aria-selected on the item.

Markdown.name: Markdown
Markdown.description: Renders a markdown string as Pharos-styled components. Use Markdown for user-generated content, AI responses, and documentation; it handles headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and citations with consistent styling.

bestPractices.description: Set headingLevelStart to match the page hierarchy, e.g. start at 3 if the markdown sits inside an h2 section.
Use contentWidth to keep prose at a readable line length in wide layouts.
Use inlinePlugins for custom shorthand patterns like issue refs, diff refs, and mentions instead of preprocessing the markdown string.
Use Markdown for hand-authored layouts; use Text and Heading directly when you control the content.

props.name: children
props.description: The markdown string to render.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Markdown defaults to block. Use 'inline' for markdown spans embedded inside text.

props.name: density
props.description: Controls spacing between block-level elements.

props.name: headingLevelStart
props.description: The HTML heading level that markdown # maps to. Shifts all heading levels down to fit the surrounding page hierarchy. Levels exceeding h6 are clamped to h6.

props.name: isStreaming
props.description: Enables streaming mode; it uses incremental parsing and a smooth fade-in animation for chunk-by-chunk text delivery.

props.name: onLinkClick
props.description: Handler for link clicks. Return false to prevent the default navigation behavior.

props.name: sources
props.description: Citation sources keyed by ID. When provided, [id] and 【id】 markers in the markdown that match a key are rendered as citation chips.

props.name: citationStyle
props.description: How citations are displayed inline. 'label' shows a chip with source title, icon, and border. 'number' shows a compact numbered badge.

props.name: contentWidth
props.description: Max width for prose content (paragraphs, headings, lists, blockquotes). Tables and code blocks are unconstrained and can expand to the full container width. Use for readable line lengths in wide layouts.

props.name: contentAlign
props.description: Alignment of prose content within the container when contentWidth is narrower than the available space.

props.name: inlinePlugins
props.description: Transforms regex matches in parsed text nodes into custom inline React elements. Use for issue refs, diff refs, mentions, and other shorthand patterns. Inline code and fenced code blocks are unaffected.

props.name: autolink
props.description: Opt-in autolinking of bare URLs and emails. 'gfm' applies GitHub-Flavored Markdown autolink-literal rules: bare https?://..., www...., <scheme:url>, <email>, and user@host all become links. Trailing sentence punctuation and unbalanced trailing close-parens are excluded; matches inside code spans, code blocks, existing links, and image alt text are skipped. Default behavior (option unset) is unchanged.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

MediaTheme.name: MediaTheme
MediaTheme.description: Provides token overrides for content rendered on inverted surfaces: media overlays, scrims, toasts, and tooltips. The base behavior flips color-scheme so all light-dark() tokens resolve to the correct side. Only a small set of tokens need explicit overrides beyond that. Themes can further customize component appearance on media surfaces via onDark/onLight in defineTheme(), with both token overrides (e.g. "--color-accent": "#90CAF9") and component overrides (e.g. ghost buttons get a border on dark surfaces).

bestPractices.description: Use for any content placed over a dark background (image overlays, video scrims, dark cards) or other inverted surfaces like toasts and tooltips.
Pair with a background color: MediaTheme flips the token context but does not add a background. Set backgroundColor on the parent element.
Themes can customize components on media surfaces via onDark.components and onLight.components in defineTheme(). For example, add a border to ghost buttons on dark surfaces.
Use MediaTheme for app-level dark mode: use Theme with mode="dark" or mode="system" instead. MediaTheme is for local surface inversions, not page-wide color scheme.

props.name: mode
props.description: Surface luminance context: dark for content over dark backgrounds (light text, white-tinted interactions), light for content over light backgrounds (dark text, black-tinted interactions).

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with inverted token context. Components inherit the correct colors automatically.

MetadataList.name: MetadataList
MetadataList.description: MetadataList displays key-value pairs for object attributes like quality, condition, and status, in a structured layout. Use it for detail panels, settings summaries, and record information.

bestPractices.description: Choose label position based on content: "start" for short values, "top" for long or complex values.
Collapse long lists with `maxNumOfItems` to keep the page scannable.
Use for extensive form input; use a form layout instead.
Use for data that doesn't have a clear key-value structure.

props.name: children
props.description: Metadata items (MetadataListItem components).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column layout mode.

props.name: label
props.description: Label display configuration. position controls label placement, width sets a custom label column width. Defaults to { position: 'top' } for multi-column layouts.

props.name: maxNumOfItems
props.description: Maximum items to show before collapsing with a show more/less toggle.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout orientation. Horizontal mode flows items in a row with flex-wrap.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional title or heading above the list.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

MetadataListItem.name: MetadataListItem
MetadataListItem.description: A single labeled metadata value within an MetadataList.

props.name: children
props.description: Content value for this metadata item.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for this metadata item.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon rendered before the label text.

MobileNav.name: MobileNav
MobileNav.description: A slide-out drawer for mobile navigation. MobileNav is the mobile counterpart to SideNav and accepts the same children. Use it on narrow viewports where a persistent sidebar is not practical. Inside AppShell, use MobileNavToggle as the trigger; it reads state from context automatically.

bestPractices.description: Share the same nav items between MobileNav and SideNav by extracting them into a variable.
Provide a header when the drawer's purpose is not obvious from its content.
Inside AppShell, use MobileNavToggle to open the drawer; it reads state from context. Do not pass isOpen/onOpenChange to the toggle.
Use MobileNav on desktop: use a persistent SideNav instead.

MoreMenu.name: MoreMenu
MoreMenu.description: MoreMenu is a three-dot button that opens a list of actions. Use it for secondary actions that don't need to be always visible, like in table rows, card headers, or toolbars.

bestPractices.description: Use for overflow or secondary actions; keep primary actions visible outside the menu.
Use dividers or sections to group related actions when the menu has many items.
Hide primary actions inside a MoreMenu; they should be directly visible.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items: data array of actions, dividers, and sections. Same type as DropdownMenu items prop.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the trigger button (aria-label) and tooltip text.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant of the trigger button.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the trigger button.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the default three-dot icon. Accepts any ReactNode.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the menu trigger is disabled.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

MultiSelector.name: MultiSelector
MultiSelector.description: A checkbox dropdown for selecting multiple values from a list. Selected items can display as a count, labels, or badges. Use it for filtering or when presenting a finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.

bestPractices.description: Use for a moderate, finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.
Enable search filtering when the list exceeds ~15 options.
Use renderOption for custom option rows; the checkbox affordance remains owned by MultiSelector.
Enable select-all when most users will want all or nearly all options selected.
Use inside InputGroup only when the control needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface; prefer count or labels trigger display so the group stays single-line.
Use for single-value selection; use Selector instead.
Show more than ~20 options without enabling search.
Wrap a disabled MultiSelector in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

NavIcon.name: NavIcon
NavIcon.description: NavIcon is a circular icon container with an accent-colored background. Use it in navigation headers such as TopNavHeading and PageNavHeader to visually identify a section or application.

bestPractices.description: Use in navigation headers to provide a recognizable visual anchor for the section.
Pass an Icon or similarly sized icon component to ensure proper proportions.
Use NavIcon for interactive purposes; it is a display-only container, not a button.

props.name: icon
props.description: The icon element to render inside the circular background. Should be an Icon or similar icon component.

NumberInput.name: NumberInput
NumberInput.description: A form input for numeric values with built-in validation, min/max constraints, and step controls. Use NumberInput for quantities, measurements, percentages, and similar inputs.

bestPractices.description: Set min, max, and step to guide users toward valid values.
Show units (e.g. "%" or "GB") so users know what the number represents.
Use NumberInput for free-form text that happens to contain numbers; use TextInput instead.
Set both isOptional and isRequired on the same field.
Wrap a disabled NumberInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when input value changes (only on valid input).

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hide the label (still accessible to screen readers).

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional (mutually exclusive with isRequired).

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the field is required (mutually exclusive with isOptional).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the input is disabled.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled NumberInput in Tooltip.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text to display in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon to display before the label text. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status with optional message.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum value allowed.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value allowed.

props.name: step
props.description: Step increment for the input.

props.name: units
props.description: Units text to display at the end of the input (e.g., "%" or "GB").

props.name: isIntegerOnly
props.description: Only allow integer values (no floating point).

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when the input has a value. When true, the onChange callback also accepts null to signal the user cleared the input.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: HTML name attribute for form submissions.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: HTML autocomplete attribute.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Whether to focus the input on mount.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the input receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the input loses focus.

props.name: onEnter
props.description: Callback fired when the user presses the Enter key.

Outline.name: Outline
Outline.description: A table-of-contents sidebar for documentation pages, help centers, wikis, and long settings pages. Use it for navigation within a single page, not for app routes. Features a sliding indicator track that animates to the active heading. The list is a single tab stop: arrow keys move between headings, Home/End jump to the ends, and Enter/Space activate.

bestPractices.description: Pass a flat ordered list of headings and let level control indentation.
Use activeId when custom scroll logic owns the active section.
Use density="compact" in dense sidebars where vertical space is tight.
Use useOutlineFromMarkdown or useOutlineFromDOM when headings are generated from content.
Pass scrollContainerRef when the content scrolls in a split pane, modal, or panel instead of the viewport.
Set offset to the height of a fixed header that overlays the content, so headings land below it instead of underneath it.
Use Outline for application navigation - use SideNav or TopNav for routes.
Use Outline for expandable hierarchy - use TreeList when nodes need expand and collapse.
Rely on onNavigateEnd to mean "arrived" - it also fires when the user interrupts the scroll.

OverflowList.name: OverflowList
OverflowList.description: A horizontal list that automatically hides items when they exceed the available width. Use OverflowList for breadcrumbs, toolbars, tag lists, or any row that needs to collapse gracefully at smaller sizes.

bestPractices.description: Provide a meaningful overflowRenderer: a "+N more" badge, a dropdown, or a count indicator.
Set minVisibleItems to keep key items visible, and maxVisibleItems to cap the row at a fixed count regardless of available width.
Use maxRows to let items wrap onto a bounded number of rows (e.g. a two-row tag cloud) before collapsing the rest into the indicator.
Use OverflowList for a vertical stack; horizontal multi-row wrap is supported via maxRows, but items still flow left-to-right, not top-to-bottom.

props.name: children
props.description: Items to render. Each child should be a single element.

props.name: overflowRenderer
props.description: Render function for the overflow indicator. Receives the list of hidden items (each with child and index). Only called when items are overflowing.

props.name: gap
props.description: Gap between items as a spacing token step (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10).

props.name: minVisibleItems
props.description: Minimum number of items to always show, even when overflowing.

props.name: maxVisibleItems
props.description: Maximum number of items to ever show, even when they all fit. The ceiling partner to minVisibleItems; extra items collapse into the overflow indicator. If less than minVisibleItems, the floor wins.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: Wrap items across up to this many rows before collapsing the rest into the overflow indicator. A number, not a boolean. Leave undefined (or set 1) for single-line behavior. Assumes uniform row height.

props.name: collapseFrom
props.description: Which end to collapse items from when overflow occurs.

props.name: behavior
props.description: Controls which element is measured for available width. 'observeSelf' uses the container's own width. 'observeParent' observes the parent element, useful when the list should stay content-sized while still detecting available space.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object.

Overlay.name: Overlay
Overlay.description: Overlay layers action or supporting content over media, cards, video, or other bounded surfaces with an optional scrim and reveal behavior.

bestPractices.description: Use overlays for short, contextual actions or labels that belong directly to the underlying media or surface.
Keep overlay content compact so it remains legible over the scrim and does not obscure important visual information.
Do not use Overlay for floating content anchored outside the surface. Use Popover, Tooltip, or Dialog for those patterns.

props.name: content
props.description: Content rendered inside the overlay scrim.

props.name: children
props.description: Base content such as an image, video, card, or media surface that the overlay sits on top of.

props.name: showOn
props.description: Visibility trigger. Hover mode also reveals on focus for keyboard accessibility; hover-or-focus is an alias for hover.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled visibility override. When set, this takes precedence over showOn and touch toggle behavior.

props.name: scrim
props.description: Scrim background mode. Set to false to render overlay content without a scrim background.

props.name: position
props.description: Where the scrim appears within the base surface.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the overlay content within the scrim.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name(s) appended to the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling when possible.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the root element. Prefer xstyle for design-system styling.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the overlay root element.

Pagination.name: Pagination
Pagination.description: Pagination lets users step through pages of content. Place it below a table, list, or card grid so users can move forward and backward through results. Pick a variant to match the context: numbered pages for data tables, a count for large lists, compact for tight spaces, or dots for carousels.

bestPractices.description: Place pagination below the content it controls so users see results before navigating.
Use the pages variant for data tables where users need to jump to a specific page.
Use the count variant with a page size selector when users need to control how many items they see at once.
Use the dots variant for carousels and walkthroughs where the total is small and position matters more than a number.
Pass totalItems when the total is known so users can see how much content remains.
Show pagination when all items fit on a single page; there is nothing to paginate.
Use the dots variant for more than about 10 pages; the dots become too small to be useful.
Place pagination above the content; users expect it at the bottom.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page number (1-based). Page 1 is the first page.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the page changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action on page change. Fires after onChange and uses React transitions for built-in loading state.

props.name: totalItems
props.description: Total number of items. Used to calculate page count. Takes precedence over totalPages if both provided.

props.name: totalPages
props.description: Total number of pages. Use when you know page count but not item count.

props.name: hasMore
props.description: Whether more pages exist after the current one. Use for cursor-based pagination where total is unknown.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Number of items per page. Coerced to a positive integer; non-finite values fall back to the default.

props.name: pageSizeOptions
props.description: Available page size options. Shows a page size selector dropdown when provided.

props.name: onPageSizeChange
props.description: Called when the page size changes. Automatically resets to page 1.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual variant controlling what appears between prev/next buttons. 'pages' shows page number buttons with ellipsis, 'count' shows 'X-Y of Z' text, 'compact' shows 'Page X of Y', 'dots' shows dot indicators, 'none' shows just prev/next buttons.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: Number of page buttons to show on each side of the current page. Only applies when variant='pages'.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the pagination controls.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the component is disabled.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Popover.name: Popover
Popover.description: A click-triggered overlay anchored to a button or trigger element. Use it for secondary actions, inline confirmations, or supplementary information that does not warrant a full dialog. For hover previews use HoverCard, for brief helper text use Tooltip.

Provide a clear way to close: either by clicking outside or with an explicit close button.
Nest popovers inside other popovers; it creates confusing focus and navigation.
Use a popover for content that requires heavy user input; use a Dialog instead.

PowerSearch.name: PowerSearch
PowerSearch.description: PowerSearch is a structured filter bar where each token represents a field, operator, and value. Use it for complex multi-dimensional filtering when users need to combine multiple search criteria. For simple single-field search, use a text input instead.

bestPractices.description: Define clear, descriptive field names and aliases so users can quickly find the filter they need.
Provide a result count to give users feedback on how their filters affect the data set.
Use PowerSearch for simple keyword searches; a standard text input is more appropriate for single-field lookups.
Wrap a disabled PowerSearch in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

ProgressBar.name: ProgressBar

Choose a color variant that matches the context: accent for general progress, success for completion, warning or error for alerts.

Use clear, concise labels that differentiate each option at a glance.

Add dividers between same-background sections that need separation.

SegmentedControl.name: SegmentedControl
SegmentedControl.description: A segmented button group that allows users to make a single selection from a small set of mutually exclusive options. Use SegmentedControl when all options should be visible at once and the selection controls a value or mode, not page navigation.

bestPractices.description: Use for switching between 2–5 mutually exclusive views or modes where all options should be visible.
Provide a descriptive label for the control to ensure the group is accessible to screen readers.
Use for page-level navigation; use TabList instead. TabList is a navigation component, while SegmentedControl is an input that always has exactly one selected option.
Use for simple on/off states; use ToggleButton instead. ToggleButton can be toggled on or off independently, while SegmentedControl enforces a single selection from a group.
