Use StackItem with size="fill" to make one item stretch and fill the leftover space.
Nest stacks inside stacks; try wrap="wrap" first to let items flow to the next line.

StatusDot.name: StatusDot
StatusDot.description: A small colored dot that communicates status like online/offline presence or severity levels. Supports five semantic variants and an optional pulse animation. Always pair with a visible text label, as color alone should not carry meaning.

bestPractices.description: Always pair with a visible text label so status is not conveyed by color alone.
Provide a descriptive `label` prop for screen reader accessibility.
Use the pulse animation for purely decorative purposes; reserve it for states that require immediate attention.
Rely on color alone to communicate status; always include text.

props.name: variant
props.description: Semantic color variant.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label surfaced via aria-label.

props.name: isPulsing
props.description: Enables a pulse animation; respects prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover to explain the status meaning.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Switch.name: Switch
Switch.description: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead.

bestPractices.description: Use for settings that apply immediately; the toggle should take effect without a separate save action.
Pair with a clear, concise label that describes the setting being controlled.
Use for options that require a form submission to take effect; use a checkbox instead.
Use a switch for multi-state values; it's strictly on/off.
Wrap a disabled switch in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <input> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the switch (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the switch is on or off.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the switch state changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Triggers optimistic UI and shows a loading spinner until the promise resolves.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the switch is in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the thumb.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the switch is disabled.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant controlling track and thumb dimensions. sm (32x20px) matches sm checkbox/radio vertical rhythm; md (40x24px, default) matches md checkbox/radio vertical rhythm.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the underlying checkbox input, useful for form submissions (submits "on" when the switch is on).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the switch is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the switch focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Switch in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the switch is required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator with type and message. Displays a colored message box below the switch and sets aria-invalid when type is "error".

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the switch receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the switch loses focus.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon displayed before the label text. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Which side of the switch the label appears on. "start" places the label before the switch.

props.name: labelSpacing
props.description: Spacing behavior between label and switch. "hug" places them next to each other; "spread" pushes them to opposite ends of the container (full width). "default" is a deprecated alias for "hug".

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

Tab.name: Tab
Tab.description: Individual tab item that renders as a button or an anchor link, with selected-state styling and optional icons.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value for this tab, matched against TabListContext.value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for this tab. Used as visible text by default, or as aria-label when isLabelHidden is true.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether the label is visually hidden. When true, only the icon and endContent are displayed, and label is used as aria-label for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: URL to navigate to; when provided, the tab renders as an anchor element.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a> for link tabs. Overrides the LinkProvider default. Only applies when href is provided.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is not selected.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is selected; falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label, such as a badge count or status dot.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TabList.name: TabList
TabList.description: TabList provides tab-style navigation for organizing content into categorized sections. Use it to let users switch between related views without leaving the page, with overflow items handled by a built-in "more" menu.

bestPractices.description: Keep tab labels short and descriptive so users can quickly scan available sections.
Use TabMenu to group overflow items when horizontal space is limited rather than scrolling tabs off-screen.

When using hasDivider with action buttons alongside tabs, match the Button size to the TabList size (both md, both sm); the divided tab strip reserves space so tabs and same-size buttons align to a shared baseline above the rail.
Use tabs for sequential steps or workflows; use a stepper or wizard pattern instead.
Place more than 6–8 visible tabs before the overflow menu; prioritize the most important categories.

Confuse TabList with SegmentedControl or ToggleButton. TabList is for navigation between views. SegmentedControl and ToggleButton are input controls: SegmentedControl always has exactly one selected option, while ToggleButton can be toggled on or off.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected tab value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a tab is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant applied to all child tabs.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout mode for tab sizing. 'hug': each tab hugs its content width. 'fill': tabs stretch equally to fill the container width.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Whether to show a bottom border divider under the tab list.

props.name: children
props.description: Tab and TabMenu items to render inside the nav.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TabMenu.name: TabMenu
TabMenu.description: Overflow menu trigger that opens a dropdown of additional tab options, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text.

props.name: label
props.description: Label for the trigger button (shown when no option is selected) and the dropdown heading divider.

props.name: options
props.description: Array of menu options rendered in the dropdown.

Table.name: Table
Table.description: Table displays structured data in rows and columns with consistent dimensionality. It supports rich cell content, sorting, selection, pagination, and column management through a composable plugin system. Use Table for data sets with uniform structure; for simpler or inconsistent data, consider a list or card layout instead.

bestPractices.description: Use density and divider variants to match the information density and scanning needs of your data.
Compose rich cell content with Pharos components like Badge, StatusDot, and Avatar via renderCell.

Set explicit width on every column using proportional() or pixel(). proportional(1) gives equal flex distribution with a 120px minimum that prevents columns from collapsing on narrow viewports. Omitting width skips the minimum.

Use the data-driven API from React Server Components: proportional(), pixel(), and column definitions without function props are server-safe. Columns using renderCell (or any function prop) need the table wrapped in a "use client" component, since functions cannot cross the server-client boundary.
Use a table for data without consistent columns. Use a list or card layout for heterogeneous content.
Enable every plugin at once. Add only the features your use case requires to keep the interface focused.
Omit width on text-heavy columns; without an explicit proportional() width they have no minimum and can squish to near-zero on mobile.

props.name: data
props.description: Array of data items to render as rows. T must extend Record<string, unknown> (use `interface MyRow extends Record<string, unknown>` for custom types).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions: each column has {key, header, width?, align?, renderCell?}. The `header` field sets the column heading text. If omitted, columns are auto-generated from data object keys. The `width` field is typed as `ColumnWidth` (not a number); use `proportional(n)` or `pixel(n)` helpers imported from `@pharos-ds/core/Table`. Example: `width: pixel(120)` for 120px fixed, `width: proportional(1)` for flex distribution.

props.name: idKey
props.description: Row key for React reconciliation. Pass a property name string or a function. Falls back to row index if omitted.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density controlling cell padding and font size.

props.name: dividers
props.description: Divider style rendered between cells.

props.name: isStriped
props.description: Applies a background wash to even-numbered rows.

props.name: hasHover
props.description: Applies a hover highlight background to rows on pointer devices.

props.name: verticalAlign
props.description: Vertical alignment for body row cells. Controls `vertical-align` on the `<td>` elements.

props.name: textOverflow
props.description: How body cell text behaves when it exceeds the column width. 'wrap' lets text wrap and the row grow taller; 'truncate' clips with an ellipsis (default-rendered cells show a tooltip on hover when truncated). Header cells always truncate.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Named plugins that extend table behavior via the transform pipeline. Converted to an ordered array internally.

props.name: rowIndexStart
props.description: ARIA row index (1-based) for the first rendered body row. The row ordinal is an accessibility concern independent of any visible index column, so setting this (or rowCount) makes the table emit aria-rowindex on body rows and aria-rowcount on the table. For a paginated/windowed view, pass the offset of the first visible row (e.g. (page - 1) * pageSize + 1) so aria-rowindex reflects position in the full dataset. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: Total number of body rows across all pages/windows, used for aria-rowcount so assistive tech can announce "row X of Y" against the full dataset. When omitted but rowIndexStart is set (windowed view with an unknown total), aria-rowcount is set to -1 per the ARIA unknown-count convention. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: children
props.description: Children mode: render TableRow/TableCell directly instead of using data-driven rendering.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TableCell.name: TableCell
TableCell.description: <td> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, font size, and divider borders when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Cell content.

TableHeaderCell.name: TableHeaderCell
TableHeaderCell.description: <th> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, semibold weight, secondary text color, and divider borders when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Header cell content.

TableRow.name: TableRow
TableRow.description: <tr> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply striped, hover, and divider styles when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Row cell elements.

Text.name: Text
Text.description: Text renders styled body text and headings from the theme. Use Text with a semantic type for body copy, labels, and captions, and Heading for section titles that output the correct h1–h6 element.

bestPractices.description: Pick a semantic type (body, label, supporting, large, code) instead of manually setting size and weight; the theme handles the details.
Set accessibilityLevel on Heading when the visual level differs from the document outline so screen readers announce the correct hierarchy.
Use maxLines with a number to truncate long content; a tooltip appears automatically on hover so no text is lost.
Enable hasTabularNumbers for columns of numeric data so digits align vertically across rows.
Override size and weight when a semantic type already matches; extra overrides fight the theme and break when themes change.
Skip heading levels in the document outline; go h1 then h2 then h3, never h1 then h3.

Use raw HTML tags like

,

–

, or for text; Text and Heading apply the correct theme tokens automatically.
Pass a `variant` prop; Text does not have a `variant` prop. Use `type` for semantic styling (body, label, large, supporting, code) or use Heading for headings.
Use Text for headings; use Heading with a `level` prop (1–6) for section titles and headings.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type. Determines size, weight, and line-height from the theme. 'inherit' takes all three from the surrounding text instead. Themes may add custom types. Note: this prop is called `type`, not `variant`.

props.name: children
props.description: Text content.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from `type` but preserves other type properties. Prefer using `type` alone.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Defaults to 'secondary' for the 'supporting' type, 'primary' for all others.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Silently overridden to 'block' when maxLines > 0 or hasCapsize is true.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum lines before truncation. 0 means no truncation. When set, shows a tooltip on hover if content is truncated.

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: Controls tooltip behavior for truncated text. true shows the tooltip at the default position, false disables it, or a placement string ('above' | 'below' | 'start' | 'end') sets a specific position.

props.name: wordBreak
props.description: Word break behavior when truncating. Defaults to 'break-all' for single-line truncation, 'break-word' otherwise.

props.name: textWrap
props.description: Text wrapping behavior.

props.name: justify
props.description: Text alignment (justification). Uses logical values (start/end) for i18n/RTL compatibility.

props.name: hasCapsize
props.description: Enable optical alignment using text-box-trim. Forces block display.

props.name: hasStrikethrough
props.description: Apply strikethrough text decoration.

props.name: hasTabularNumbers
props.description: Use tabular (monospace) numbers for aligned numeric data.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TextArea.name: TextArea
TextArea.description: TextArea is a multi-line text input for collecting longer-form content like comments, descriptions, or messages. Use it when the expected input spans multiple lines. For shorter, single-line values, use TextInput.

bestPractices.description: Provide a visible label so users know what to enter. If the label must be hidden, set isLabelHidden with a descriptive label for screen readers.
Set maxLength with a character counter when there is a defined limit; it helps users stay within bounds before they submit.
Use the status prop to surface validation feedback inline: show success when input is valid, warning for soft limits, and error for hard failures.
Add a description or placeholder to clarify expected content, like "Describe the issue in detail," but never rely on placeholder alone as the only label.
Avoid using TextArea for short, single-line values like names or emails; use TextInput instead.
Don't rely solely on placeholder text to communicate the purpose of the field; placeholders disappear on focus and are not accessible labels.
Don't show a status message without also setting the status type; the colored border and icon are what draw the user's attention to the message.
Don't wrap a disabled TextArea in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <textarea> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the textarea. Always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the textarea.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange inside a React transition. Enables optimistic updates via useOptimistic.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed between the label and textarea.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the textarea, preventing interaction.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the textarea is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the textarea focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextArea in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the textarea in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the input.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the textarea is empty.

props.name: rows
props.description: Number of visible text rows.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Maximum number of characters allowed. When set, a character counter (current/max) is displayed below the textarea. Does not enforce the limit natively; the counter shows error styling when exceeded.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that applies a colored border and icon. An optional message is displayed in a floating box below the textarea.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon component rendered inside the leading edge of the textarea wrapper. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: hasSpellCheck
props.description: Enables or disables browser spell checking.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the textarea on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the textarea, affecting internal padding. Height is controlled by rows, not size.

props.name: onPaste
props.description: Callback fired when content is pasted into the textarea.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: HTML name attribute for the textarea element, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea loses focus.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TextInput.name: TextInput
TextInput.description: TextInput collects short-form text like names, emails, or search queries. Use it for single-line values where the expected input is brief. Pair it with validation status to guide users through required or formatted fields.

bestPractices.description: Always provide a visible label so users know what the field is for. Only hide the label when surrounding context makes it obvious, like a search bar with a magnifying-glass icon.
Use validation status with a message to explain what went wrong: "Email must include @" is better than just turning the border red.
Size the input to match the expected content length so users can gauge how much to type: small for zip codes, medium for names, large for URLs.
Add a clear button for search and filter inputs so users can quickly reset without selecting all text.
Don't use placeholder text as a replacement for a label; placeholders disappear on focus and are not reliably read by screen readers.
Don't use TextInput for multi-line content like comments or descriptions; use TextArea instead.
Don't mark every field as required; only flag mandatory fields so users are not overwhelmed by validation errors.
Don't wrap a disabled TextInput in Tooltip to explain why it's disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: type
props.description: The HTML input type.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input: always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the input value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange (if not prevented). Triggers optimistic update and shows a loading spinner while pending.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant of the input.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextInput in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: SVG icon component displayed at the start of the input. See `pharos docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border and status icon. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when the input has a value. Clicking it clears the value and returns focus to the input.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the input on mount.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the input, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

Theme.name: Theme

bestPractices.description: Build app themes that are known ahead of time with `pharos theme build`, then import the generated CSS and built theme object.
Use runtime themes when the theme is created or edited in the browser, such as theme editors, user branding, or prototypes.
Token names always start with `--` (e.g. `--color-accent`, `--color-background-surface`). Do not omit the prefix.
Default to runtime themes in SSR production apps. Component overrides inject after hydration instead of shipping as static CSS.

props.name: theme
props.description: Theme object to apply. Prefer built theme objects for static production themes; use runtime `defineTheme()` for dynamic themes.

props.name: mode
props.description: Color mode. System follows OS preference.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the theme.

Thumbnail.name: Thumbnail
Thumbnail.description: Thumbnail displays a compact, square preview of an image attachment. It shows a shimmer effect while uploading, the image on success, and a placeholder icon when no source is set. Use it in chat composers, file upload lists, or anywhere you need a small image preview with optional remove and click actions.

bestPractices.description: Always provide a label prop with the file name so the thumbnail and its remove button are accessible to screen readers and show a tooltip on hover.
Use isLoading without a src to show a skeleton during initial upload, and isLoading with a src to show a spinner overlay once a preview URL is available.
Pair onClick with a lightbox or detail view so users can inspect the full image; the thumbnail adds button semantics and a hover overlay automatically.
Don't use Thumbnail for non-image file types like PDFs or spreadsheets; use a file attachment component with an appropriate icon instead.
Don't omit alt text when a src is provided; screen readers need a description of the image content, not just the file name from label.

props.name: src
props.description: Image source URL.

props.name: alt
props.description: Alt text for the image. When omitted, the image is explicitly decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden) and hidden from screen readers; a dev warning fires if neither alt nor label is set.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label (e.g. file name). Shown as tooltip on hover.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback for the overlaid remove button.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. Adds button semantics and a hover overlay.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows skeleton (no src) or upload overlay (with src).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the thumbnail is disabled.

props.name: showRemoveOn
props.description: When the remove button is visible. `hover` (the default) reveals it on hover and on keyboard focus, and keeps it visible on any touch-capable device; `always` shows it at rest. Only applies when `onRemove` is set.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

TimeInput.name: TimeInput
TimeInput.description: TimeInput lets users enter a time of day and converts it to a standard format. It also allows users to adjust times using the arrow keys. Use it in forms, scheduling flows, or any interface where users need to select a specific time.

bestPractices.description: Choose the hour format (12h or 24h) that matches your audience's locale: 12-hour with AM/PM for US-centric UIs, 24-hour for international or technical contexts.
Set min and max constraints when the context has a valid range, like business hours or event windows, so users cannot submit an out-of-bounds time.
Provide a description or placeholder that hints at the expected format or purpose, like "Business hours: 9 AM – 5 PM".
Use the status prop to surface validation errors inline: show a message like "Time must be during business hours" so users know exactly what to fix.
Enable hasClear when the field is optional, so users can remove a previously selected time.
Place TimeInput inside InputGroup when the time needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon, like a start/end label or timezone marker.
Don't use TimeInput for combined date-and-time selection; pair it with a separate DateInput instead.
Don't hide the label; even when space is tight, keep the label visible or provide a description so the purpose is clear.
Wrap a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input (required for accessibility).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an "(optional)" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and suppresses interactions.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the field focusable via aria-disabled (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled time value in ISO format (HH:MM or HH:MM:SS).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the time changes. Receives undefined when the input is cleared.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Wrapped in a React transition to provide optimistic UI; triggers the loading spinner while pending.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input into a loading state, displaying a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: hasSeconds
props.description: Includes seconds in the time display and parsing.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a value is set and the input is not disabled.

props.name: hourFormat
props.description: Controls the display format. '12h' shows AM/PM (e.g. '2:30 PM'); '24h' uses 24-hour notation (e.g. '14:30').

props.name: increment
props.description: Number of minutes to add or subtract when the user presses the up or down arrow key.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no time is selected. When the input is focused and empty, a format hint overrides this text.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls the height of the input element.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that colors the border and displays an icon. When a message is provided it is rendered below the input.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text rendered as an info icon at the end of the label row.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Timestamp.name: Timestamp
Timestamp.description: Timestamp formats a date or time value into human-readable text. Use it to show when something was created, updated, or is scheduled; picking relative for recency, absolute for precision, or auto to let the component decide.

bestPractices.description: Use the auto format in feeds and lists so recent items show "2 hours ago" and older items show the full date automatically.
Keep formatting consistent within the same list or table; mixing relative and absolute timestamps in the same column confuses scanning.
Enable isTimezoneShown when the audience spans multiple time zones, like a global team calendar or audit log.
Use tooltipEntries when readers must compare zones, such as an incident log where the reader's time and the event's origin zone both matter.
Label every entry once a tooltip shows more than one zone; a bare abbreviation is not always recognizable (Tokyo renders as "GMT+9", not "JST").
Use isLive for active dashboards or real-time feeds so the relative time stays accurate without a page refresh.
Don't display raw Unix timestamps or ISO strings to users; always pass them through Timestamp to get a human-readable format.
Avoid system_date or system_time formats in user-facing UI; they are meant for developer tools, logs, and machine-readable contexts.
Don't disable the tooltip on relative timestamps; users expect to hover for the full date when they see "3 hours ago".
Don't stack many zones into one tooltip; it is capped at 300px wide and long labelled lines wrap. Two or three entries read well.

Don't pass a fixed-offset abbreviation like "EST" as timezoneID; it is a valid identifier but never observes daylight saving, so it reads an hour wrong for half the year. Use the region id, "America/New_York".

props.name: value
props.description: The date/time to display. Accepts Unix timestamps (seconds) or ISO 8601 strings.

props.name: format
props.description: Display format. 'relative' shows '2 hours ago', 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2025', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2025', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2025', 'date_time' shows 'Mar 21, 2025, 2:51 PM', 'time' shows '2:51 PM', 'system_*' variants use ISO-style formatting, 'auto' switches from relative to date_time based on recency.

props.name: autoThreshold
props.description: Threshold in seconds for 'auto' format to switch from relative to date_time.

props.name: hasTooltip
props.description: Whether to show a tooltip with the full date/time on hover when displaying relative time.

props.name: tooltipEntries
props.type: ReadonlyArray<{timezoneID?: string; format?: TimestampTooltipFormat; label?: string}>
props.description: Lines to show in the hover tooltip, so one instant can be read in several time zones and/or formats at once. Each entry is one line, in the order given. Omit timezoneID (or pass 'local') for the viewer's own zone; format defaults to the full absolute style and also accepts 'full' alongside every non-relative TimestampFormat. Configuring entries also attaches the tooltip to absolute formats, which otherwise have none.

props.name: isTimezoneShown
props.description: Whether to append the timezone abbreviation to the visible text. Applies to the date_time and time formats; system_* formats stay machine-readable and never carry one. Use tooltipEntries to control the tooltip’s time zones.

props.name: isLive
props.description: Whether the relative time should update live (e.g. "2 min ago" → "3 min ago").

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type from Text. Determines size, weight, and line-height.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from type.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

Toast.name: Toast
Toast.description:
Toast shows a brief, non-blocking notification to confirm an action or present temporary information. Use it for scenarios where the user needs feedback but not a decision, such as saving, deleting, or changing a status.

For production use, prefer the `useToast()` hook; it handles positioning, stacking, auto-dismiss, and deduplication via `ToastViewport`. The `Toast` component renders the visual toast element inline and is useful for previews, documentation, and static showcases where the viewport lifecycle is not needed.

bestPractices.description: Keep messages short: only a few words that tell the user what happened, like "Changes saved" or "Message sent".
Add an undo action in the endContent slot for reversible operations like deleting an item, so the user can recover without navigating away.
Use uniqueID to deduplicate toasts that fire from repeated actions, like clicking a save button multiple times.
Use error type for failures that need attention but not immediate action; it persists until dismissed so the user won't miss it.
Don't use a toast for critical errors that block the user. Use Banner for persistent, in-context messaging that requires acknowledgment.
Don't put long or multi-line content in a toast; it disappears after 5 seconds and the user may not finish reading.
Don't show form validation errors as toasts. Use inline field validation so the user can see exactly which field needs fixing.

props.name: body
props.description: Primary message content.

props.name: type
props.description: Toast type controlling background color. Error toasts persist until dismissed.

props.name: isAutoHide
props.description: Whether the toast auto-dismisses. Defaults to true for info, false for error.

props.name: autoHideDuration
props.description: Duration in ms before auto-dismiss.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing end (e.g. Undo button, link).

props.name: uniqueID
props.description: Unique identifier for deduplication.

props.name: collisionBehavior
props.description: Behavior when a toast with matching uniqueID already exists.

props.name: onHide
props.description: Callback fired when the toast is removed.

ToggleButton.name: ToggleButton
ToggleButton.description: ToggleButton switches between selected and unselected states to represent a persistent on/off choice. Use it standalone for binary actions like bold, mute, or favorite, or inside a ToggleButtonGroup for single-select or multi-select toolbar controls.

bestPractices.description: Use a filled or colored icon for the pressed state so users can see the current state at a glance: an outline star vs a solid star, for example.
Keep the label identical between pressed and unpressed states. Let the visual treatment (icon, weight, background) communicate the change.
Wrap related toggles in a ToggleButtonGroup with an accessible label so screen readers announce them as a connected set.
Don't use a ToggleButton for one-time actions like "Submit" or "Delete"; those are regular Buttons, not toggles.
Don't mix ToggleButtons with regular Buttons inside the same group; use only ToggleButtons in a ToggleButtonGroup.
Don't use a ToggleButton for on/off settings that persist across sessions; use a Switch instead, which better communicates "setting" semantics.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the button. Used as visible text, or as aria-label for icon-only buttons.

props.name: isPressed
props.description: Whether the button is currently pressed. Ignored when inside a group.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Called when pressed state should change. Receives the next state and the click event; call event.preventDefault() to skip pressedChangeAction. Ignored when inside a group.

props.name: pressedChangeAction
props.description: Action handler for API- or navigation-backed toggles, run in a transition. Shows an optimistic pressed state immediately and a spinner while pending; the button stays interruptible by re-clicks.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Defaults to group size when inside a group.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the button shows a loading spinner.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element. When provided without children, button becomes icon-only with tooltip from label.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: When true, renders as a square icon-only button with `label` as the aria-label and an automatic tooltip from the label.

props.name: pressedIcon
props.description: Icon shown when pressed. Falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: children
props.description: Visible content. If omitted with icon, button becomes icon-only.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

props.name: value
props.description: Value identifier when used inside ToggleButtonGroup. Required in groups.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

ToggleButtonGroup.name: ToggleButtonGroup
ToggleButtonGroup.description: Groups toggle buttons for exclusive (single) or multi-select behavior. Uses discriminated union on type for type-safe value/onChange.

props.name: children
props.description: ToggleButton children.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group (aria-label).

props.name: type
props.description: Selection mode. Single allows one active button, multiple allows many.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected value(s). Type depends on selection mode.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the button group.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for buttons in the group. Individual buttons can override.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all buttons in the group are disabled.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

Token.name: Token
Token.description: Token is a small, inline element for representing discrete pieces of associated data, like tags, categories, or selections. Use it to label content, show active filters, or represent removable items like selected recipients in a compose field.

bestPractices.description: Use color to distinguish categories (for example, green for "Active", red for "Blocked", blue for "In Review") so users can scan status at a glance.
Provide an onRemove callback when tokens represent user selections that can be undone, like filters or multi-select values.
Add a leading icon when it helps identify the token type faster, like a person icon for user tokens or a tag icon for labels.
Keep labels short: one to three words. Tokens truncate with ellipsis when the text overflows.
Don't use tokens for primary actions or navigation; use Button or Link instead. Tokens are for displaying metadata, not triggering workflows.
Don't hide the label unless the icon alone is universally understood. A color dot without text is ambiguous.
Don't mix too many colors in one token group. Stick to two or three meaningful colors so the palette stays scannable.

props.name: label
props.description: Text label displayed inside the token.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the token.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant of the token.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon rendered before the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the token is disabled; reduces opacity and blocks interactions.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback fired when the remove button is clicked. When provided, an X button is rendered inside the token.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. When provided, the token renders as a <span> container with an invisible <button> inside for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL. When provided, the token renders as an <a> element.

props.name: description
props.description: Accessible description applied via aria-description on the root element.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label and before the remove button.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label using a screen-reader-only clip technique; the label remains accessible.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Tokenizer.name: Tokenizer
Tokenizer.description: Tokenizer is a multi-select input that lets users search, select, and manage multiple items displayed as removable chips. Use it when users need to build a set of selections from a searchable data source, like adding team members, applying tags, or choosing filters.

bestPractices.description: Write a placeholder that tells users what they can search for, such as "Search people..." or "Add tags...", so the input is not a blank mystery.
Set maxEntries when the number of selections should be bounded, like limiting a review to 5 approvers.
Use hasCreate for free-form tagging where users need to enter values that do not exist in the search source.
Show validation status with the status prop so users know immediately when a selection is missing or invalid.
Don't use Tokenizer for single-item selection; use Typeahead instead. Tokenizer is for building sets of two or more items.
Avoid applying custom colors to individual tokens inside a Tokenizer; use the default token style for visual consistency across the set.
Don't hide the label; every Tokenizer needs a visible label so users understand what they are selecting. Use isLabelHidden only when surrounding context makes the purpose obvious.
Wrap a disabled Tokenizer in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled controls swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the input.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods for populating the dropdown.

props.name: value
props.description: Array of currently selected items.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes. The change argument includes the affected item and type ('add' | 'create' | 'remove' | 'reorder'). Additions and removals (including Backspace on an empty input) are announced to screen readers via a polite live region.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text. Only shown when no tokens are selected.

props.name: maxEntries
props.description: Maximum number of selections allowed. Input is hidden when the limit is reached.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show a clear-all button for bulk removal of all tokens.

props.name: renderToken
props.description: Custom render function for selected tokens. Default renders Token with label and onRemove.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items. Default renders TypeaheadItem.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and all token interactions.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders one hidden input per selected item id.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the tokenizer is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (input stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Tokenizer in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and message for error/warning/success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an optional indicator on the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on the label.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of dropdown items to display.

props.name: emptySearchResultsText
props.description: Text shown when search returns no results.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Input and token size.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources.

props.name: hasCreate
props.description: Allow users to create new tokens from free-text input. When true, a "Create" option appears in the dropdown for typed text that doesn't match existing results. The onChange change type is 'create' for these items.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input, before any tokens. Accepts a semantic icon name, an SVG icon component, or a ReactNode directly.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to display at the end of the input row. Useful for buttons, result counts, or other controls.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle exposing focusInput(), focusFirstToken(), focusLastToken(), clearInput(), and selectAll().

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value; not an inline style object like style={{}}.

Toolbar.name: Toolbar
Toolbar.description: Toolbar is a horizontal bar with left, center, and right areas. Use it for contextual actions within a content area (above a table, inside a card, or in a panel), not as a page-level header. Set the size once on the toolbar and all buttons, inputs, and tabs inside it match automatically.

bestPractices.description: Put secondary actions like "Back" on the left, and primary actions like "Save" on the right.
Make temporary toolbars like bulk selection visually distinct so users can tell they're contextual, for example with a background color or border.
Visually separate the toolbar from the content below it, with a divider, a background variant, or both.

Use Toolbar as a card header when the header has interactive actions like filter or add; it gives you slot layout, keyboard navigation, and size cascading. If the header is just a title with no actions, a LayoutHeader or Section is enough.
Put too many actions in one toolbar; move less common items into a MoreMenu.
Set size on individual child buttons; set it once on the toolbar and it cascades automatically.
Use Toolbar for app-wide navigation like main menu links or sign out; use TopNav or LayoutHeader for that.

Tooltip.name: Tooltip
Tooltip.description: A short text hint that appears on hover or focus, anchored to a trigger element. Use it to describe icon-only buttons, show the full text of truncated labels, or provide supplementary context without cluttering the UI.

bestPractices.description: Keep tooltip content concise: aim for under 140 characters of plain text.
Add a tooltip to icon-only buttons and controls that lack a visible label.
Place interactive elements like links or buttons inside a tooltip; use HoverCard or Popover instead.
Use tooltips for essential information that users must see to complete a task.

TopNav.name: TopNav
TopNav.description: TopNav is a horizontal navigation bar for product-level navigation in application headers. Use TopNav for 5 or fewer always-visible navigation items, or minimal navigation paired with search and controls. For complex navigation hierarchies, use a sidebar; to filter content, use tabs or filter buttons instead.

bestPractices.description: Include a product logo and name in the heading slot to clearly identify the application.
Limit primary navigation items to 5 or fewer for quick scanning and minimal cognitive load.
Avoid using TopNav to filter page content; use Tabs or filter controls instead.
Avoid deeply nested navigation hierarchies; keep menus to one level of depth.

props.name: heading
props.description: Heading slot content (logo, brand): positioned at the left edge of the nav bar.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Start content slot for navigation items or breadcrumbs: positioned after the heading, left-aligned.

props.name: children
props.description: Alias for startContent. Prefer startContent when composing with heading, centerContent, or endContent; children keeps the common React nav-item pattern from silently dropping items.

props.name: centerContent
props.description: Center content slot (tabs, search bar, primary navigation): when provided, switches the layout to a three-column CSS grid for true horizontal centering.

props.name: endContent
props.description: End content slot for search, icons, or user profile: positioned at the right edge.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark, applied as aria-label on the <nav> element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TopNavHeading.name: TopNavHeading
TopNavHeading.description: Product/suite/account heading for the TopNav heading slot. Supports smart interaction boundary logic: logo, heading text, superheading/subheading with independent links, and an optional menu popover with automatic chevron indicator.

props.name: logo
props.description: Logo element to display before the heading text. Can be an image, NavIcon, or any ReactNode.

props.name: heading
props.description: Product/app name displayed as the primary heading text.

props.name: headingHref
props.description: Link for the heading text (e.g. product home). When no menu is present and this is the only href, the whole heading becomes one clickable link.

props.name: href
props.description: Deprecated: use headingHref instead. URL to navigate to when clicked.

props.name: superheading
props.description: Text above the heading (e.g. suite name). Rendered in a smaller secondary style.

props.name: superheadingHref
props.description: Link for the superheading text (e.g. suite home). When provided alongside a menu, renders as an independent inline link.

props.name: subheading
props.description: Text below the heading (e.g. account context). Rendered in a smaller secondary style.

props.name: subheadingHref
props.description: Link for the subheading text. When provided alongside a menu, renders as an independent inline link.

props.name: headerEndContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing edge of the heading row (e.g. a badge or status indicator).

props.name: menu
props.description: Menu content shown in a popover dropdown. When provided, a chevron indicator appears automatically. Interaction boundary is determined by the presence of hrefs: no hrefs means the whole header is the trigger; with hrefs, links are independent and the chevron area is the trigger.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider. Must accept href, className, style, and children props.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value.

TopNavItem.name: TopNavItem
TopNavItem.description: Navigation link item for use in TopNav startContent: renders as an anchor with hover and selected states.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the nav item. Rendered as visible text by default. When isIconOnly is true, used as aria-label instead.

props.name: href
props.description: Navigation target URL.

props.name: isSelected
props.description: Whether this nav item is currently selected. Sets aria-current="page" and applies highlighted styles.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the nav item is disabled. Sets aria-disabled, drops href/target so the item cannot navigate, and prevents interaction.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: Renders the item as a square icon-only element. When true, label becomes the aria-label and visible text is hidden. Requires icon to be set.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon to display before the label.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content to render instead of the label text.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a>. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider. Must accept href, className, style, and children props.

TopNavMegaMenu.name: TopNavMegaMenu
TopNavMegaMenu.description: Navigation item that displays a full-width mega menu panel on hover. Uses a slots API with items and featured props. TopNavMegaMenuItem renders itself in both desktop and mobile drawer modes. Supports inline collapsible drawer via render mode context.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for the trigger button.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items slot: typically TopNavMegaMenuItem components, but accepts any ReactNode.

props.name: featured
props.description: Featured content slot: rendered in the right panel on desktop, below items in the mobile drawer.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before showing the menu on hover.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before hiding the menu after the mouse leaves.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when the mega menu opens or closes. Useful for coordinating wrapper styles.

TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard.name: TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard
TopNavMegaMenuFeaturedCard.description: Standard featured card for the TopNavMegaMenu featured slot. Provides a consistent card with optional image, title, description, and CTA link.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text below the title.

props.name: image
props.description: Optional image URL displayed above the body.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Alt text for the image. When omitted, the image is explicitly decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden), usually correct since the card already has a visible title. Provide it only when the image conveys information beyond the title and description.

props.name: linkLabel
props.description: CTA link text.

props.name: linkHref
props.description: CTA link URL.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content rendered below the standard body.

TopNavMegaMenuItem.name: TopNavMegaMenuItem
TopNavMegaMenuItem.description: An individual item inside an TopNavMegaMenu. Renders itself in both desktop (popover grid) and mobile drawer modes via render mode context.

props.name: title
props.description: Display title for the menu item.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description text displayed below the title.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon element displayed to the left.

props.name: href
props.description: URL to navigate to when clicked.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Callback when item is clicked.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a> for link items. Overrides the provider-level default set by LinkProvider.

TopNavMenu.name: TopNavMenu
TopNavMenu.description: Navigation item that displays a hover-triggered popover menu with rich items containing an icon, title, and optional description.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for the trigger button.

props.name: items
props.description: Menu items to display in the hover popover.

props.name: delay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before showing the menu on hover.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Delay in milliseconds before hiding the menu after the mouse leaves.

TreeList.name: TreeList
TreeList.description: An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships.

bestPractices.description: Provide meaningful labels and icons for each node to make the hierarchy easy to scan.
Pre-expand important branches so users see key content immediately.
Nest more than 4–5 levels deep; flatten the structure or use a different pattern.
Use a tree for flat, non-hierarchical data; use a List instead.

Typeahead.name: Typeahead
Typeahead.description: A searchable input for selecting a single item from a large or dynamic dataset. Results appear as the user types, with support for async data sources, debounced search, and custom item rendering. Use it when the option list is too large for a Selector dropdown.

bestPractices.description: Provide descriptive placeholder text that hints at what users can search for.
Show suggestions on focus when users benefit from seeing popular or recent options before typing.
Add a search delay for remote data sources to avoid excessive network requests.
Use inside InputGroup when the typeahead needs a single-line prefix or suffix addon.
Use for short, static option lists; use Selector for better discoverability.
Use for multi-selection; use Tokenizer instead.
Place multiple Typeaheads adjacent to each other without clear labels differentiating them.
Wrap a disabled Typeahead in Tooltip to explain why it is disabled; disabled triggers swallow the hover events the wrapper needs. Use the disabledMessage prop instead.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the input.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods for populating the dropdown.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected item, or null if nothing is selected.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when the selection changes.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show clear button to deselect the current value.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the field focusable via aria-disabled (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Typeahead in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of dropdown items to display.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and message for error/warning/success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items. Default renders TypeaheadItem.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an optional indicator on the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on the label.

props.name: emptySearchResultsText
props.description: Text shown when search returns no results.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Input and token size.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback when the dropdown opens or closes.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

TypeaheadItem.name: TypeaheadItem
TypeaheadItem.description: Default dropdown item renderer for typeahead results. Shows label with optional icon, description, and avatar. Exported for use in custom renderItem implementations.

props.name: item
props.description: The search result item to render.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon or avatar to display before the label.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether this item is visually disabled.

props.name: group
props.description: Group label for grouping items visually.

VisuallyHidden.name: VisuallyHidden
VisuallyHidden.description: Renders content in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually. Use for accessible names on icon-only controls, aria-live announcement regions, and supplementary screen-reader context. Deliberately has no styling props; the whole point is to stay invisible.

bestPractices.description: Use to give icon-only buttons and controls an accessible name that screen readers announce.
Render as a block element (as="div") with aria-live to announce dynamic updates like drag-and-drop or result counts.
Use it to hide content from everyone; it stays in the accessibility tree; use conditional rendering or `hidden` to remove content entirely.
Put interactive controls inside it; the content is not visible and cannot receive pointer input.

props.name: children
props.description: Content exposed to assistive technology while hidden from sight.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML tag to render as. Use a block element for live regions.
